source.title: Emergent Ordinal Geometry in Transformers Trained on Local Comparisons

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests delayed generalization and its geometric progress measure on a synthetic local-comparison task, rather than reproducing modular-arithmetic grokking.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results from its own synthetic training runs on adjacent comparisons and held-out distant comparisons. Its pretrained-LLM results measure ordinal representations, not delayed generalization; these are recorded under fits_no_version. It also reports confidence and geometric-distance effects, which do not measure any listed grokking version.
record.test_reason: The authors train small Transformers on a synthetic local-comparison task, a small algorithmic dataset different from modular arithmetic. They report train accuracy saturating early while held-out accuracy rises later and transiently, and they track a geometric progress measure and the effect of weight decay on it. The LLM probing part does not test any grokking version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that small Transformers trained only on adjacent comparisons form a 1D rank-aligned embedding manifold. This coincides with transient, grokking-like OOD generalization. A minimum-norm account predicts the geometry, including end-anchoring. Confidence and geometric separation scale with rank distance, mirroring the symbolic distance effect. A pretrained 1.5B LLM shows similar but domain-specific, layer-stable ordinal geometry: linear for sizes and digits, weaker and cyclic for months. All of these observations are described as correlational.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a synthetic hidden total order and trains only on adjacent comparisons, rather than modular arithmetic. The paper uses a single-layer Transformer, AdamW, and weight decay.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that unregularized runs never organize, and that the synthetic structured solution degrades after its peak under fixed weight decay. No exact λ values or systematic outcome differences among the swept λ values are stated.

fits_no_version.finding: Pretrained Qwen2.5-1.5B shows domain-dependent rank-aligned geometry: digits r≈0.81 on PC2, sizes moderate, months r=0.41. It is layer-stable, and domain probe directions are nearly orthogonal.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Ordinal concepts in pretrained LLMs lie on approximately linear, rank-aligned, domain-specific axes whose linearity tracks how total the order is.

record.problems: The synthetic results are described qualitatively, and many plotted values are not stated numerically in the text. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The experiments use one small Transformer setup and three chain lengths, with the training-set-size delay trend not isolated. Analyses use the peak-OOD checkpoint, and the authors describe both the synthetic and LLM observations as correlational.

untested.parts: Delay growing as the training set shrinks. N changes chain length and train size together, and no delay-vs-size result is reported. Whether accuracy reaches near-perfect is not stated numerically.
Identification of a generalizing circuit, removal of memorizing components, and whether the progress measure precedes the jump.
Efficiency comparison of generalizing and memorizing solutions, critical dataset size, and ungrokking.
Not tested; the LLM is probed only.

missing.what: Statement that d=64 was used 'for reliable grokking' with N>15, implying grokking was unreliable at d=32 for larger chains (a capacity sensitivity)
Numerical peak OOD accuracy, onset step of generalization, and swept λ values are not given in the text. Rows cannot be quantified.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. The task is algorithmic but not modular arithmetic, so T2. All synthetic dynamics are figure-only, with no numbers or uncertainty. The theory explicitly excludes the trajectory and grokking dynamics. The transient nature of the generalization contrasts with stable grokking in the originals.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not establish that the delay grows as the training set shrinks; its N=10, 15, and 20 runs change chain length and training-set size together, with no reported delay-versus-size comparison.

It tracks embedding linearity, but does not identify a generalizing circuit, measure removal of memorizing components, or show that a continuous measure anticipates rather than accompanies the generalization rise.
No delayed-generalization experiment on non-algorithmic training data, or initialization-scale or weight-norm switch between lazy and rich behavior, is reported.
The pretrained LLM is probed observationally; the paper does not measure delayed generalization during LLM pretraining or fine-tuning.

The paper argues for a minimum-norm ordinal solution and reports that unregularized runs do not organize, but does not compare the efficiency of generalizing and memorizing circuits, identify a critical dataset size, or test ungrokking below it.
No comparison of learned algorithms across runs on the same task is reported.
No optimizer-instability or floating-point/softmax artifact control is reported.

relationships.reason: Training accuracy saturates almost immediately while held-out distant-pair accuracy rises later (r1–r6). The evidence is figure-based and qualitative.
relationships.display_finding: Training accuracy saturated almost immediately, while accuracy on held-out distant pairs rose later.

relationships.condition: Fixed weight decay, N=15 (stated for all N)
relationships.reason: The generalized solution is transient: OOD accuracy degrades after its peak (r4). Reliable grokking at N>15 needed d=64 (r6, footnote).
relationships.display_finding: Out-of-distribution accuracy declined after its peak at N=15, while reliable grokking for N>15 required d=64.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Fixed weight decay, N=15 (stated for all N)
source_check.reason: Later degradation does not contradict V1, which does not require permanent retention. The d=64 footnote concerns N>15 and provides no controlled failure result for the stated N=15 condition.

relationships.reason: The continuous geometric measure (PC1 variance) rises together with OOD accuracy rather than ahead of it (r7). It accompanies the jump but is not shown to anticipate it.
relationships.display_finding: PC1 variance rose together with OOD accuracy, accompanying the jump without a demonstrated advance signal.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: Row r7 measures geometric covariation, without identifying a generalizing circuit or memorizing-component removal. Lack of demonstrated anticipation leaves those mechanisms untested rather than establishing a scope limitation.

relationships.reason: The authors state unregularized runs never organize, while weight decay yields the rank-line solution, consistent with a low-norm bias (r9). Only geometry is reported for λ=0, not OOD accuracy.
relationships.display_finding: Weight decay produced the rank-line solution, while unregularized runs failed to organize.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.reason: Row r9 reports geometric organization only. The idealized minimum-norm argument explains preferred embedding geometry; this comparison does not measure generalization without decay or competition between efficient generalizing and memorizing circuits.

relationships.condition: Fixed weight decay over long training
relationships.reason: Under fixed weight decay the structured, generalizing solution degrades after its peak (r4, r7), so the low-norm bias does not stably keep it.
relationships.display_finding: The structured, generalizing solution degraded after its peak even though weight decay remained fixed.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Fixed weight decay over long training
source_check.reason: V5 does not assert permanent retention under fixed decay. Rows r4 and r7 show temporal degradation without testing a critical dataset size or ungrokking caused by crossing below it; the paper explicitly excludes trajectory dynamics from its minimum-norm account.
